newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says finds missing U.S. uranium.
newsitem.headline: EU says finds missing U.S. uranium.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it had found 116 kg (255 lbs) of unused uranium missing since May from a U.S. nuclear facility in Lynchburg, Virginia.

It said the uranium, which had originated in a shipment from a facility in Greifswald, Germany, was found back where it started from -- in the east German facility, which is being dismantled following the fall of the Berlin Wall.
A European Union source said the low enriched non-irradiated uranium had apparently been left in the fuel assembly when it had arrived at the Lynchburg facility as part of a larger shipment.
The Lynchburg facility is run by French company Framatome Cogema.

In a statement, the Commission, which monitors nuclear issues for the 15-nation EU through its EURATOM agency, said Framatome Cogema had received a shipment of fuel assemblies in May 1996 from the German operator.
It had later reported that a fuel assembly was missing.
Inspectors from EURATOM and the International Atomic Energy Agency found the missing uranium in an unsealed fuel assembly during a routine visit to the facility on November 14, it said.
The inspectors verified the uranium was part of the original shipment and sealed the fuel assembly.
"It does not pose a threat for public health," a Commission spokesman said.
EU Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis said the incident underlined the need for nuclear material transport regulations to be respected.
The Commission statement said the EU executive was in contact with U.S. authorities to avoid recurrence of what it called "such anomalies."
